doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Parents and Badin, the Alcoa company town
summary: Donaldson gives his parents' names, describes Badin as a company town, and says his mother was a teacher and his father a preacher and insurance salesman.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Louis Andrew Donaldson, Jr. My father, Louis Andrew Donaldson, Sr. My mother was Lucy Wallace Donaldson.
You grew up in Badin, North Carolina?
Badin. That’s right. Badin, North Carolina.
What kind of town is it?
It’s a town where they had nothing but the Alcoa Aluminum plant. Everybody in that town, unless they were doctors or lawyers or teachers or something, worked in the plant.
So it was a company town.
Were you parents from there, or had they migrated there?
My mother was from Virginia. My father was from Tennessee. But he came to North Carolina to go to college.
Which college did he go to?

The college he went to was the oldest black college... I’m trying to think of it now. But Olds-heimers has got me. Not Alzheimers. Oldsheimer’s. It was in Salisbury, North Carolina. What was that college... Can’t think of it.
You don’t have to look it up. I’ve got all that information in a book.
Maybe we can get at it tomorrow. But in any event, how old were your parents? When were they born?
They were old. What can I tell you?

Yeah, I know the birthdates. I’ve got all of that. If you need that. But they moved to Badin... My mother was a teacher. She went to Cheyney University in Pennsylvania, and she came back to this town and was a first grade teacher and music teacher, and choral director, band director, everything with music. My father was an AME Zion Methodist preacher and an insurance salesman. So we had a pretty stable family.
